Stop paying penalties for growing your business.

A1: Send to my personal / corporate email (I will specify the address in the write-in option)

In browser-based HTML, browsers cannot execute raw SMTP commands directly (connecting to port 587/465) because doing so would expose your private email and SMTP passwords in public page source code.

To have inquiries delivered to your inbox, you have two options:

---

### Option 1: Zero-Maintenance Form Endpoint (Recommended for Static Sites)
You don't need a running server. The form posts to a free handler (like [Web3Forms](https://web3forms.com) or [Formspree](https://formspree.io)) which instantly forwards the submission to your email inbox.

```html
<!-- Example in index.html -->
<form action="https://api.web3forms.com/submit" method="POST">
  <input type="hidden" name="access_key" value="YOUR_ACCESS_KEY">
  <input type="hidden" name="to_email" value="your-email@domain.com">
  <input type="hidden" name="subject" value="New 48-Hour Stack Audit Inquiry">
  <!-- form fields -->
</form>
```

---

### Option 2: Dedicated Node.js / Python SMTP Micro-service
If you have private SMTP credentials (e.g., via Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, AWS SES, or your cPanel/host SMTP):
* We create a lightweight 30-line Node.js or Python backend in `website/server/`.
* Your SMTP credentials (`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`) are protected inside a private `.env` file.
* When someone clicks submit on `index.html`, it `fetch()`es your local/cloud endpoint and dispatches the email to your recipient address.

---

### Next Step
**Please share:**
1. What email address should receive the audit inquiries?
2. Do you have an existing SMTP provider (e.g., Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, cPanel, AWS SES), or would you prefer a zero-server endpoint like Web3Forms/Formspree?

Here is a direct critique of **`"Charlton Earl Smith | Systems & Efficiency Partner"`**:

---

### What Works Exceptionally Well (The Wins)

1. **"Systems & Efficiency Partner" is gold.**
   * The word **"Partner"** immediately elevates you above a software vendor or freelance contractor. A vendor sells a product; a *Partner* sits on the same side of the table as the CEO/COO and takes ownership of outcomes.
   * **"Systems & Efficiency"** focuses 100% on the result rather than the tech. It tells the business owner: *"I make things run smoothly, eliminate busywork, and save your team time."*
2. **Matching your Domain & Personal Brand**:
   * It aligns seamlessly with **[charltonearlsmith.co.za](https://charltonearlsmith.co.za)**. It sounds distinguished, senior, and authoritative.

---

### The Subtle Friction Points (What to Watch Out For)

1. **Name Redundancy on LinkedIn**:
   On your LinkedIn profile page, your name is already displayed in large bold text right above the headline:
   ```text
   Charlton Earl Smith
   Charlton Earl Smith | Systems & Efficiency Partner
   ```
   Repeating your name in the headline burns the first 20 characters of the most valuable visual real estate.

2. **The "Comment Feed" Truncation**:
   When you leave a comment on someone's post, LinkedIn only displays your name followed by the first ~40 characters of your headline:
   * **How it looks now**:  
     `Charlton Earl Smith • Charlton Earl Smith | Systems & Effi...`  
     *(Your name appears twice, and the reader barely sees the word "Efficiency" before it cuts off).*
   * **How it looks if you lead with the role**:  
     `Charlton Earl Smith • Systems & Efficiency Partner @ Cha...`  
     *(Your value and role are visible instantly).*

3. **Solo Freelancer vs. Institutional Practice**:
   * `Systems & Efficiency Partner` standing alone can sometimes read like a solo freelancer or contractor.
   * Adding an entity anchor (e.g. `Partner @ Charlton Earl Smith` or `Principal @ Charlton Earl Smith Operations`) positions you as an **institutional delivery firm** capable of taking on $15k–$25k turnkey implementations and managed retainers.

---

### 3 Ways to Polish and Elevate It

#### 🌟 Polish 1: Lead with the Role (Highest Feed Impact)
> **Systems & Efficiency Partner @ Charlton Earl Smith | Mid-Market Operations & Automation**
* **In the comment feed**: `Charlton Earl Smith • Systems & Efficiency Partner @ Charlton Earl...`
* **Why it works**: Solves the name duplication while keeping your exact title and firm name.

---

#### 💼 Polish 2: The Executive Managing Partner
> **Managing Partner @ Charlton Earl Smith | Systems & Efficiency for Growing Businesses**
* **In the comment feed**: `Charlton Earl Smith • Managing Partner @ Charlton Earl Smith...`
* **Why it works**: Matches Tobi Oluwole's executive cadence (`[Executive Role] @ [Firm] | [Specialty]`).

---

#### ⚡ Polish 3: Ultra-Minimalist & Direct (No fluff)
> **Systems & Efficiency Partner | Eliminating Operational Friction for Mid-Market Companies**
* **In the comment feed**: `Charlton Earl Smith • Systems & Efficiency Partner | Eliminating...`
* **Why it works**: Direct, zero redundancy, and hooks anyone struggling with operational bottlenecks.

---

### Recommendation
If you love **"Charlton Earl Smith"** and **"Systems & Efficiency Partner"**, go with **Polish 1**:
> **`Systems & Efficiency Partner @ Charlton Earl Smith | Mid-Market Operations & Automation`**

It keeps your exact preferred identity, reinforces your domain name, and avoids repeating your name twice on your profile.

				#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Deploy Metabase OSS on Google Cloud Run
set -euo pipefail

PROJECT_ID="${1:-myanalyticsproduct}"
REGION="${2:-europe-west1}"
CLOUD_SQL_INSTANCE="${3:-myanalyticsproduct:europe-west1:scbi-ducklake-catalog}"
: "${METABASE_DB_PASSWORD:?METABASE_DB_PASSWORD is not set. Export it from Secret Manager entry 'metabase-db-password' before deploying.}"
# Direct VPC egress. Without it this service has no route to a private address at all, so its
# connection to the Cube SQL runtime (deploy_cube_sql_vm.sh, internal IP only, no external
# address) fails at the TCP layer before any credential is checked -- and the failure looks
# identical to a wrong password in the Metabase UI.
#
# `private-ranges-only` keeps public traffic on Cloud Run's own egress path, so only RFC 1918
# destinations are routed through the VPC. Sending everything through the VPC instead would need
# a Cloud NAT for Metabase to reach the internet.
VPC_NETWORK="${VPC_NETWORK:-default}"
VPC_SUBNET="${VPC_SUBNET:-default}"

echo "Deploying Metabase OSS to Cloud Run in ${REGION}..."

gcloud run deploy scbi-metabase \
    --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
    --image="metabase/metabase:latest" \
    --region="${REGION}" \
    --platform=managed \
    --memory="2Gi" \
    --cpu="2" \
    --min-instances=0 \
    --max-instances=5 \
    --set-env-vars="MB_DB_TYPE=postgres,MB_DB_DBNAME=metabase_appdb,MB_DB_PORT=5432,MB_DB_USER=metabase_admin,MB_DB_HOST=/cloudsql/${CLOUD_SQL_INSTANCE},MB_DB_PASS=${METABASE_DB_PASSWORD}" \
    --add-cloudsql-instances="${CLOUD_SQL_INSTANCE}"     --network="${VPC_NETWORK}"     --subnet="${VPC_SUBNET}"     --vpc-egress=private-ranges-only \
    --allow-unauthenticated

echo "Metabase deployed successfully on Cloud Run!"

**Container not running at all.** Almost always a module-load throw. `cube.js` has five of them:
`assertAllowlistsResolve()`, three `requireEnv` calls, `assertApiSecretIsUsable()`,
`parseSqlUsers()` and `assertSqlApiIsCoherent()`. Each names what is wrong and why:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh scbi-cube-sql --zone=europe-west1-b --tunnel-through-iap \
    --command='sudo docker logs $(sudo docker ps -aq --latest)'
```

**Authentication failed.** The password is checked with scrypt against the digest in
`CUBEJS_SQL_USERS`. An unknown username costs the same work as a known one, deliberately, so the
store cannot be probed by timing â€” "authentication failed" does not tell you which half was wrong.
Re-mint (Â§2) and redeploy; there is no way to recover a password from a digest.

**Connects, but a cube is missing.** That is the role boundary working. `queryRewrite` restricts
each login to its role's `allowedCubes` â€” see the table in Â§2. The answer is the right connection
for that domain, not a wider role.

---

## 8. Rotation

Re-running `mint_sql_users.js` mints new passwords and takes every existing connection down until
Metabase and Power BI are updated. Rotate deliberately, one domain at a time if the dashboards are
in use:

```bash
node cube/mint_sql_users.js quotations     # just this domain
```

Then merge that entry into the existing `CUBEJS_SQL_USERS` value, redeploy, and update the one
Metabase database that uses it.

				FROM cubejs/cube:latest

WORKDIR /cube/conf

COPY package.json ./
RUN npm install --production

COPY . .

# Set environment defaults
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV CUBEJS_DB_TYPE=duckdb
ENV CUBEJS_PORT=4000
ENV CUBEJS_DEV_MODE=false

# US-8.3: the Postgres wire protocol (SQL API) port. The variable Cube reads is
# CUBEJS_PG_SQL_PORT. This image previously set CUBEJS_SQL_PORT, which is not a Cube variable --
# it binds nothing, so the SQL API was never listening on any runtime built from this image and
# every Metabase and Power BI connection was refused at the TCP layer. cube.js now refuses to
# start on that configuration; see assertSqlApiIsCoherent().
ENV CUBEJS_PG_SQL_PORT=5432

# 4000 is the REST/GraphQL API. 5432 is the SQL API.
#
# Cloud Run serves 4000 only: it routes a single container port and speaks HTTP/1, HTTP/2, gRPC
# and WebSockets, so the raw-TCP Postgres wire protocol cannot reach a Cloud Run service at any
# port. One image, two runtimes -- cube/deploy_cube_rest_cloudrun.sh for the REST half that the
# thin web app calls, cube/deploy_cube_sql_vm.sh for the TCP half that Metabase and Power BI
# connect to. docs/METABASE_CUBE_SQL.md covers the split.
EXPOSE 4000 5432

CMD ["npm", "run", "start"]

"# LinkedIn Post: The $1,000 BI System That Beat an $80K Enterprise Stack
**Author:** Charlton Earl Smith | Systems & Efficiency Partner @ Appleify Automation  
**Format:** High-Impact Text Post (Tobi Oluwole Style)  
**Target Audience:** Mid-Market E-Commerce Founders, COOs, VPs of Finance & Operations  

---

His sales were growing fast across Shopify, Amazon, and Wholesale.

But his executive team was flying blind.

To get simple daily metrics—gross margin by channel, customer repeat purchase rates, regional fulfillment bottlenecks—his team was spending 18 hours every week copying numbers between spreadsheets.

He went to market for enterprise business intelligence.

The quote he received from an enterprise vendor:
• $38,000 / year for a cloud data warehouse (Snowflake)
• $24,000 / year for per-seat BI licenses (Power BI / Looker)
• $18,000 / year for ETL pipeline connectors (Fivetran)
• Plus a $25,000 implementation fee from a consulting agency.

Total first-year bill: **Over $100,000.**

His board told him: *"We have zero budget for this right now. Make the spreadsheets work."*

---

Here is what most software vendors will never tell you:

You do not need a $100,000 software stack to get sub-second executive dashboards.

Software companies charge you per user, per query, and per data sync because their business model depends on recurring software drag.

Your business model depends on delivering products your customers love.

I made him an offer:
*"Give me 48 hours. I will build and demonstrate a private-cloud BI system that handles your millions of transactions in real-time, gives your CEO a live dashboard every morning, and costs under $1,000 to run."*

---

"import urllib.request
import json
import time

BASE = "http://localhost:3000"

def get_session():
    data = json.dumps({
        "username": "charltonsmithfde@gmail.com",
        "password": "Password123!"
    }).encode("utf-8")
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{BASE}/api/session", data=data, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode())["id"]

def test_api():
    session_id = get_session()
    print(f"Session established: {session_id[:12]}...")

    # Get databases
    req = urllib.request.Request(f"{BASE}/api/database", headers={"X-Metabase-Session": session_id})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        db_list = json.loads(resp.read().decode())
        print(f"Databases count: {len(db_list.get('data', []))}")
        target_db_id = None
        for db in db_list.get("data", []):
            print(f"  ID: {db.get('id')}, Name: '{db.get('name')}', Engine: {db.get('engine')}")
            if "Cube" in db.get("name", ""):
                target_db_id = db.get("id")

    if not target_db_id:
        print("Cube database not found in list, checking raw data:")
        print(json.dumps(db_list, indent=2))

server.py - Thin Web App Server (Target Enterprise Architecture)

Pure API proxy and presentation server connecting directly to Google Cloud Run (scbi-cube).
ZERO embedded DuckDB engine.
ZERO GCS access keys.
ZERO local database files.
All analytical compute and semantic definitions reside in scbi-cube.
"""

import os
import sys
import json
import time
import datetime
import urllib.request
import urllib.parse
import http.server
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import jwt
except ImportError:
    jwt = None

WEB_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PORT = 8080
CUBE_BASE_URL = os.environ.get("CUBEJS_BASE_URL", "https://scbi-cube-886154918734.europe-west1.run.app")
def require_env(name: str) -> str:
    """US-2.2: a missing credential is a startup failure, never a silent
    downgrade to an in-code default."""
    value = os.environ.get(name)
    if not value:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"{name} is not set. Provide it from Secret Manager "
            f"(Cloud Run: --set-secrets {name}=<secret-entry>:latest). "
            f"Locally, set it user-level so a fresh shell inherits it."
        )
    return value


CUBE_SECRET = require_env("CUBEJS_API_SECRET")

# US-1.3 criterion 3. Once scbi-cube is deployed --no-allow-unauthenticated, Cloud Run demands a
# Google-signed ID token for the service. Cube needs its own HS256 token on the same request, so
# the ID token travels on X-Serverless-Authorization: Cloud Run authenticates that header and
# leaves Authorization untouched for the application behind it.
#
# Unset means no ID token is attached, which is correct only while scbi-cube still allows
# unauthenticated invocation. Setting it is what opts in, so this half can ship before the
# infrastructure half without breaking either. The value is the Cube service's own URL.
CUBE_ID_TOKEN_AUDIENCE = os.environ.get("SCBI_CUBE_ID_TOKEN_AUDIENCE")
# The GCE / Cloud Run metadata server. SCBI_METADATA_BASE_URL exists so the acceptance suite can
# stand in for it, and is not a bypass: unset, the real metadata server is the only source, and a
# token that cannot be obtained fails the request rather than downgrading it.
METADATA_BASE_URL = os.environ.get("SCBI_METADATA_BASE_URL", "http://metadata.google.internal")
METADATA_IDENTITY_PATH = "/computeMetadata/v1/instance/service-accounts/default/identity"
_ID_TOKEN_CACHE = {"token": None, "fetched_at": 0.0}
# Metadata ID tokens live an hour; re-mint at the halfway mark. A dashboard page load issues
# eight or more Cube calls, so minting per call would be eight metadata round trips per view.
_ID_TOKEN_TTL_SEC = 1800

# US-1.1: the IAP audience this service accepts. Cloud Run sets it to
# /projects/<project-number>/apps/<project-id> (or the backend-service form for
# a load balancer). A wrong or missing audience must be a startup failure, not
# a token that verifies against the wrong app.
IAP_AUDIENCE = require_env("SCBI_IAP_AUDIENCE")
# Google's real JWKS. SCBI_IAP_JWKS_URL overrides *which issuer's keys* are
# trusted so the acceptance suite can mint its own; it is not an auth bypass --
# signature, aud, iss and exp are still fully verified against whatever it
# points at. Production sets no such variable.
IAP_JWKS_URL = os.environ.get("SCBI_IAP_JWKS_URL",
                              "https://www.gstatic.com/iap/verify/public_key-jwk")
IAP_ISSUER = "https://cloud.google.com/iap"
_JWKS_CACHE = {"keys": None, "fetched_at": 0.0}
_JWKS_TTL_SEC = 3600
# Query execution log buffer for telemetry
_QUERY_BUFFER = []

Connects to Cube.js Semantic Layer & serves the executive cosmetic analytics portal.
Mathematical Scaling Applied:
  - Values divided by 1,000 (R 7.42B -> R 7.43M GMV)
  - Member & Order counts divided by 100 (1.47M -> 14,738 customers; 29.2M -> 292,093 orders)
  - Funnel sessions divided by 100 (129,954 -> 1,299 abandoned sessions)
"""

import os
import sys
import json
import time
import urllib.request
import urllib.parse
from http.server import HTTPServer, SimpleHTTPRequestHandler

WEB_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PORT = int(os.environ.get("PORT", 8085))
CUBE_SQL_URL = os.environ.get("CUBE_URL", "http://localhost:4000")

class ThinWebAppHandler(SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, directory=str(WEB_DIR), **kwargs)

    def do_GET(self):
        parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(self.path)
        path = parsed.path

        if path == "/api/v1/health":

                "status": "healthy",

## Prompts

**dbt Cloud.** With 300+ jobs, 8 developers, and a stage/intermediate/mart/product structure, model-build volume will likely exceed the Starter plan's 5 seats and 15K models per month. You would likely need Enterprise, which is custom-priced and usually negotiated at $50K to $120K per year.

**Fabric capacity.** For 100 to 200 consumers I assumed an F64, which lets viewers read content without individual Pro licences. A semantic model fed by 800 GB of marts also needs real capacity. Reserved pricing is roughly $60K per year, and pay-as-you-go is roughly $100K. A cheaper pattern is an F32 with Pro licences for all 200 consumers, which costs similar money but is less scalable.

**Ingestion tooling.** Not specified in the brief. Snowpipe or COPY from cloud storage costs almost nothing extra. A managed connector like Fivetran at 10 to 50 TB can add $40K to $80K or more. I included a middle allowance, which is the largest uncertainty in the table.

A New York e-commerce founder DM’d me last week.

His store does $7M in sales.

Sounds impressive.

Until he told me his net profit is in the low hundreds of thousands.

He was bleeding margin.

His biggest headache? 

Cart abandonment was spiking, and he had no idea why.

He didn’t have a BI team.

He was running the company on default Shopify exports and Amazon Seller Central CSVs.

Every vendor he spoke to quoted him the exact same playbook:

Snowflake. dbt Cloud. Fivetran. Power BI.

Price tag: $210,000/year in SaaS. 

Plus another $160,000 for a data engineer in New York to maintain it.

That alone would have wiped out his entire year’s profit.

He had no budget for software licenses. 

He didn’t need enterprise hype. 

He needed answers before his next board meeting.

I told him: “Give me 5 days.”

We didn’t buy a single software license.

We didn’t hire anyone new.

We set up an out-of-the-box architecture using Google Cloud Storage, DuckDB, Cube, and Metabase.

In 5 days, he had a live executive dashboard scanning his entire order history in 1.11 seconds.

Total software cost: $0.

Cloud hosting: under $100/month.

Next week, we are upskilling his 2 existing technical staff to maintain it.

I hope his board gives approval for this to be a full case study I can share with you.

Swipe through the carousel below to see how we bypassed the $300k SaaS trap. ⬇️

---

**Hashtags**: #Ecommerce #BusinessIntelligence #Profitability #Operations #Startups #DataEngineering
"

args.CodeContent:
"# LinkedIn Post Standards & Design Template

## 1. Post Text Principles
- **Length**: 8 lines at most (each line is a single punchy sentence separated by whitespace).
- **Tone**: Grounded, authentic business dilemma. No sales pitches, no "DM me", no aggressive CTA, no vendor jargon.
- **Narrative Structure**:
  1. Relatable business hook (e.g. founder outreach, real revenue scale).
  2. The financial reality / net profit context.
  3. The enterprise SaaS trap / exorbitant quote.
  4. The business threat (e.g., wiping out a third of profit).
  5. What the business actually needed (clarity, speed, reliability).
  6. The open-source / pragmatic solution & timeline (e.g. 5 days).
  7. Key operational proof (zero license fees, internal team enablement).
  8. Punchline / timeless business takeaway.

## 2. Branded Post Image Card (Tobi Oluwole Format)
- **Dimensions**: 1080 x 1350 px (4:5 portrait).
- **Background**: Solid black (`#000000`) or deep midnight.
- **Header**: Circular avatar (Charlton Smith), bold name, blue verified badge (`#1D9BF0`), subtle grey handle (`@charltonsmith`).
- **Typography**: Inter / clean modern sans-serif, bold (`font-weight: 600-700`), white (`#FFFFFF`).
- **Rhythm**: 3 short, high-contrast statements with generous whitespace (50-60px gap).
  - Statement 1: The enterprise quote or industry absurdity.
  - Statement 2: The actual business constraint or profit reality.
  - Statement 3: The pragmatic takeaway or proof.
- **Tooling**: Rendered via headless Chromium at `1080x1350`.
"
